rows.text: # Linkage and crossing over ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Linkage and crossing over** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Heredity and Evolution fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Mendel's second law assumes genes assort independently — but genes live on chromosomes, and a chromosome carries hundreds of them. Genes on the **same chromosome** tend to be inherited together: this is **linkage**, and it was proved by T. H. Morgan's work on *Drosophila* (1910–1915).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Linkage: genes on the SAME chromosome tend to inherit together, violating independent assortment; coupling phase (AB/ab) vs repulsion (Ab/aB).  ·  Trick 2: Crossing over in pachytene of prophase-I produces recombinants; recombination frequency ∝ distance between genes (1 map unit = 1% recombination).
